The **2024 NBA Finals** was the [championship series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association")'s (NBA) [2023–24 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_NBA_season "2023–24 NBA season") and conclusion to [the season's playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs "2024 NBA playoffs"). In the [best-of-seven playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best-of-seven_playoff "Best-of-seven playoff") series, starting on June 6 and concluding on June 17, the [Eastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Conference_\(NBA\) "Eastern Conference \(NBA\)") champion [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Boston_Celtics_season "2023–24 Boston Celtics season") defeated the [Western Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Conference_\(NBA\) "Western Conference \(NBA\)") champion [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Dallas_Mavericks_season "2023–24 Dallas Mavericks season") four games to one. The Celtics' [Jaylen Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown "Jaylen Brown") was voted the [NBA Finals Most Valuable Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player "NBA Finals Most Valuable Player") (MVP).
Led by [the duo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jays_\(Boston_Celtics\) "Jays \(Boston Celtics\)") of [Jayson Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") and Brown, the Celtics were seen as favorites for winning the championship, finishing with a league-best 64–18 regular season record and advancing through the playoffs with a 12–2 record.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:232-1) The fifth-seeded Mavericks built around [Luka Dončić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Don%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Luka Dončić") only became a Finals contender midway through the season after a series of roster changes.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:18-2) The Celtics won the first two games at home to start the series. In Dallas, the Celtics built a large lead in Game 3 which the Mavericks significantly narrowed in the fourth quarter before Boston pulled through with the victory. The Mavericks responded in Game 4 with one of the largest blowout victories in Finals history, but the Celtics won Game 5 in Boston decisively to claim the championship.
With the victory, the Celtics won their first championship since [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NBA_Finals "2008 NBA Finals") and their 18th overall, giving them the most championships of any franchise in the NBA. They were the sixth unique champion team in a row in what capped off a historically dominant season and playoffs. They continued to compete behind Brown and Tatum, but let go of many players from the championship team after being eliminated in the [2025 playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NBA_playoffs "2025 NBA playoffs"). Meanwhile, the Mavericks [controversially traded away Dončić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Don%C4%8Di%C4%87%E2%80%93Anthony_Davis_trade "Luka Dončić–Anthony Davis trade") the next season and entered a rebuild.
## Background
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]
This was the first playoff meeting between the Celtics and the Mavericks, as well as for all teams from the [Greater Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Boston "Greater Boston") and [Dallas–Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_metroplex "Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex") areas in any of the [four major North American sports leagues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_professional_sports_leagues_in_the_United_States_and_Canada "Major professional sports leagues in the United States and Canada").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-3) It was also the third Finals appearance for the Celtics where they played a team from [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas"), as they previously defeated the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980%E2%80%9381_Houston_Rockets_season "1980–81 Houston Rockets season") in the [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_NBA_Finals "1981 NBA Finals") and [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_NBA_Finals "1986 NBA Finals") Finals. Boston won both their meetings against Dallas in the regular season,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12222-4) and finished 14 games better than the Mavericks in the regular season.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-5) The Mavericks were the fifth team in NBA history to reach the Finals without holding home-court advantage in any round, the last team to do so being the eighth-seeded [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Miami_Heat_season "2022–23 Miami Heat season") in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NBA_Finals "2023 NBA Finals"). Out of those five, only one, the Rockets in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_NBA_Finals "1995 NBA Finals"), won the championship.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-tsn.ca-6) Had the Mavericks won, they would have become the 11th NBA team to win multiple championship titles.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:222-7)
### Boston Celtics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Boston Celtics")]
Main article: [2023–24 Boston Celtics season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Boston_Celtics_season "2023–24 Boston Celtics season")
[![Image of Joe Mazzulla with a whiteboard during a basketball game.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Celtics_at_Wizards_2024-12-046_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Celtics_at_Wizards_2024-12-046_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Celtics_at_Wizards_2024-12-046_\(cropped\).jpg)Head coach [Joe Mazzulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla "Joe Mazzulla") led the Celtics to the Finals, tying [Bill Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Russell "Bill Russell") as the youngest ever to do so.
After losing the [2022 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NBA_Finals "2022 NBA Finals") to the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Golden_State_Warriors_season "2021–22 Golden State Warriors season"), the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") were defeated in the 2023 Eastern Conference Finals in seven games after mounting a failed attempt to overcome a 3–0 series deficit.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-8) During the off-season, the Celtics were involved in a trade which sent out longtime guard [Marcus Smart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Smart "Marcus Smart") in exchange for [Kristaps Porziņģis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristaps_Porzi%C5%86%C4%A3is "Kristaps Porziņģis").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:0222-9) They also acquired defensive guard [Jrue Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jrue_Holiday "Jrue Holiday") while trading away [Robert Williams III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Williams_III "Robert Williams III"), [Malcolm Brogdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_Brogdon "Malcolm Brogdon") and two first-round draft picks.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:02-10) The retooled roster was once again led by the '[Jays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jays_\(Boston_Celtics\) "Jays \(Boston Celtics\)")',[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12222-4) the longtime duo of [Jayson Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") and [Jaylen Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown "Jaylen Brown"), with support from the [two-way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-way_player "Two-way player") backcourt of Holiday and [Derrick White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_White "Derrick White") and rotating centers Porziņģis and [Al Horford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Horford "Al Horford").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:232-1)
The Celtics prioritized [three-point-shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-point_shooting "Three-point shooting") offensively while maintaining a versatile roster of defenders.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-11) They dominated throughout the season, winning all of their first 20 games at home,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:042-12) permanently occupying the first seed position in the Eastern Conference from mid-November onwards,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:14-13) and finishing with a league-best 64–18 record;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:232-1) the highest Eastern Conference win percentage since the [2012–13 Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Miami_Heat_season "2012–13 Miami Heat season").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12-14) Boston set numerous records during the season. They had the highest offensive rating in NBA history at 123.2,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:02-10) tied the third-best net rating in NBA history at 11.6,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:322-15) the fifth-widest margin of outscoring their opponents by an average of 11.3 points per game, and the highest points per possession (1.22) in league history. They also had the widest margin of wins between the first and second seeds in the Eastern Conference since 1976 at 14 games.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:042-12)
In the first round of the playoffs, the Celtics faced the Miami Heat in a rematch of the previous year's Eastern Conference Finals, and won the series 4–1.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:232-1) They then faced the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Cleveland_Cavaliers_season "2023–24 Cleveland Cavaliers season") in the second round, again winning in five games. After sweeping the [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Indiana_Pacers_season "2023–24 Indiana Pacers season") in the Conference Finals they reached the NBA Finals.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:232-1) Due to injuries to key players on all three opposing teams during their run through the Eastern Conference playoffs, the Celtics' path to the Finals was considered by media writers as one of the easiest in NBA history.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12-14) The Celtics had the best point differential in the playoffs at plus-10, the second-best points-per-game average at 111.4 (behind the Pacers), and allowed the third-lowest points per game for their opponents with 101.3.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12222-4) Even as starting center Porziņģis, who suffered a soleus strain in Game 4 of the first round, was sidelined for the next two rounds, the Celtics went 9–1 without him.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:02-10)
This was the 23rd appearance in the NBA Finals for the Celtics, and their second in three years.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:15-16) Media commentators, analysts, and the Celtics themselves viewed the team as in a "championship or bust" scenario, implying their historically dominant season would be overshadowed if they failed to win the Finals.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:232-1)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:14-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12-14) A Finals victory would give the Celtics their 18th championship, one more than the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") for the most in NBA history. Their last victory was in the [2008 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NBA_Finals "2008 NBA Finals"),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:15-16) and before then the 1986 Finals.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-17) [Joe Mazzulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla "Joe Mazzulla"), the 35-year-old head coach appointed by the Celtics a season prior, was tied with [Bill Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Russell "Bill Russell") as the youngest coach in league history to lead a team to the finals. Russell did so for the Celtics in [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_NBA_Finals "1969 NBA Finals") as a [player-coach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player-coach "Player-coach").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:322-15) Porziņģis met his former team, the Mavericks, in the Finals, having played for them from 2019 to 2022.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-18)
### Dallas Mavericks
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Dallas Mavericks")]
Main article: [2023–24 Dallas Mavericks season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Dallas_Mavericks_season "2023–24 Dallas Mavericks season")
[![Image of Luka Dončić holding a basketball during the 2022 NBA All-Star Game.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Luka_Doncic_%2851914012202%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Luka_Doncic_%2851914012202%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Luka_Doncic_\(51914012202\)_\(cropped\).jpg)
[![Image of Kyrie Irving holding a basketball during the 2022 NBA All-Star Game.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Kyrie_Irving_%2851830909437%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Kyrie_Irving_%2851830909437%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kyrie_Irving_\(51830909437\)_\(cropped\).jpg)
Mavericks stars [Luka Dončić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Don%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Luka Dončić") (left) and [Kyrie Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrie_Irving "Kyrie Irving") (right) were praised as an elite offensive duo during [the season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Dallas_Mavericks_season "2023–24 Dallas Mavericks season").
Despite acquiring star guard [Kyrie Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrie_Irving "Kyrie Irving") at the trade deadline the prior season, the [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks") missed the [2023 NBA playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NBA_playoffs "2023 NBA playoffs") entirely after finishing as the 11th seed in the Western Conference.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-19) Over the off-season, the team reconfigured its roster to center around Irving and [Luka Dončić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Don%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Luka Dončić"), drafting [Dereck Lively II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dereck_Lively_II "Dereck Lively II") and [Olivier-Maxence Prosper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier-Maxence_Prosper "Olivier-Maxence Prosper"), and signing [Grant Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Williams_\(basketball\) "Grant Williams \(basketball\)"), [Seth Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry "Seth Curry"), [Dante Exum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dant%C3%A9_Exum "Danté Exum") and [Derrick Jones Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Jones_Jr. "Derrick Jones Jr.")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:1102-20)
Throughout the 2023–24 season, the backcourt duo of Irving and Dončić was praised by analysts as one of the greatest of all time offensively.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:14-13)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12222-4)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:02-10) Dončić was the [scoring leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NBA_annual_scoring_leaders "List of NBA annual scoring leaders") of the season and finished third in voting for [Most Valuable Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Most_Valuable_Player "NBA Most Valuable Player"), while Irving underwent what was viewed as a renaissance season, averaging 25.6 points on near [50–40–90](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50%E2%80%9340%E2%80%9390_club "50–40–90 club") shooting percentages.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:032-22) Exum and Jones Jr. provided effective 3-and-D performances,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:032-22) while Lively also played a pivotal role as a big man, making the [All-Rookie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Rookie_Team "NBA All-Rookie Team") second team and obtaining the highest field-goal percentage for a rookie season in NBA history at 74.7%.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:032-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-23) However, Dallas nonetheless struggled through the first half of the season barely above the .500 mark.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:1102-20) Until the trade deadline in February, the team was 22nd in defensive rating, 12th in offense and 17th in net rating across the league. Among other roster pieces, Irving and Dončić both missed a significant number of games during that period due to injuries.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-24)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:032-22)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:222-7)
At the trade deadline, the Mavericks made more major changes to the roster, exchanging Williams and Curry for power forward [P. J. Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Washington "P. J. Washington") and acquiring center [Daniel Gafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Gafford "Daniel Gafford"). The two players would further complement the Irving–Dončić backcourt by significantly reinforcing the team's defense into a powerhouse. The trade has been regarded as the catalyst for the Mavericks morphing into championship contenders by the next month. From March 7 onwards, the Mavericks had the best defensive rating, the 12th-best offensive rating and the fifth-best net rating in the league, and went 16–4 to end the season.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:18-2) From February 1 onwards, Dallas had a 36–15 record: the second best in the league behind the Celtics.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-tsn.ca-6) They eventually finished as the fifth seed in the Western Conference with a 50–32 overall record.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:1102-20)
In the first round of the playoffs, the Mavericks faced the [Los Angeles Clippers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Clippers "Los Angeles Clippers"), who had eliminated them in two first-round series in the five years prior. The Mavericks won the series in six games.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-25) In the second round they faced the first-seeded [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Oklahoma_City_Thunder_season "2023–24 Oklahoma City Thunder season"). The Mavericks overcame a 16-point halftime deficit in Game 6 to eliminate the Thunder, advancing to their second Western Conference Finals in three years.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-26) After defeating the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Minnesota_Timberwolves_season "2023–24 Minnesota Timberwolves season") in the first three games of the Conference Finals by a combined margin of 13 points, dropping Game 4, and winning Game 5 in a 21-point blowout,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12222-4) the Mavericks secured their first NBA Finals appearance in 13 years and their third in franchise history. In their last appearance in [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_Finals "2011 NBA Finals"), the team, which featured current head coach [Jason Kidd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Kidd "Jason Kidd") as point guard, won their first and only title.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:222-7) Like Porziņģis, Irving faced off against a former team of his, the Celtics, whom he played for from 2017 to 2019, having maintained a highly strained relationship with their fan base since his departure. Irving was a combined 0–10 against the Celtics since leaving Boston in free agency.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:12222-4)

He then scored a three-pointer as the Celtics went on a run to end the quarter at 37–20, the largest first quarter point differential in a Game 1 in NBA Finals history.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:5-30) The Celtics continued their momentum into the second quarter, going on a 21–11 run[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:5-30) and leading by as much as 29 points before Dončić went on a solo run to end the half at 63–42. [Jayson Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") (left) and [Jaylen Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown "Jaylen Brown") (right) scored 31 and 30 points respectively to secure a 3–0 series lead for the Celtics.
Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown scored 31 and 30 points to stave off a late-game Mavericks rally and put the Celtics up 3–0 in the series.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:142-42) It was the second time in franchise history that two players each scored 30-plus points in a Finals game.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-43) Tatum logged six rebounds and five assists while Brown had eight rebounds and eight assists,[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:152-44) with the victory extending Boston's playoff winning-streak to 10 and its road-game winning-streak to seven. The only other Celtic to score in double-figures was Derrick White, who had 16 points.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:162-45) Kyrie Irving led all scorers with 35 points, while Luka Dončić had 27 points, six rebounds and six assists.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:172-46) Coming into the game, the Celtics were without the injured Kristaps Porziņģis,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:162-45) who was replaced by [Al Horford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Horford "Al Horford") and occasionally [Xavier Tillman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Tillman "Xavier Tillman") at the center position. The Mavericks, specifically Irving and Dončić, took advantage of the lack of size for Boston to attack the rim,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:182-47) outscoring Boston 52–36 from the area during the game.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:192-48)
The Mavericks started strong, scoring nine points to force a timeout from the Celtics early on.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:182-47) The Mavericks heavily utilized the paint[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:192-48) to outscore the Celtics 22–9 by the midpoint of the quarter—their largest lead in the series by that point. The Celtics responded with a 21–9 run led by Brown and Tatum.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:142-42)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:182-47) The second quarter was defense-oriented at first, with the Celtics leading the scoring 5–2 at the halfway mark before Irving and Tatum began responding to each other's three-pointers,[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:142-42) ending the half at a near tie.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:152-44) The Celtics dominated the third quarter, scoring on their first seven possessions to establish an imposing lead as Brown scored half of his points in the game during the timeframe.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:182-47) After Dončić made a layup to bring the lead down to six with 5:11 remaining, the Celtics went on a 7–0 run to end the quarter with a 15-point lead, outscoring the Mavericks 35–19 in total.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:172-46)
Up until the final quarter, the Mavericks, excluding Irving and Dončić, combined for only 19 points.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-49) The Celtics initially continued their offensive momentum into the fourth quarter, capitalized by a three-pointer from White a minute in to extend the lead to 21 points.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:172-46) However, the Mavericks proceeded to go on a 22–2 run, with contributions from P. J. Washington and [Dereck Lively II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dereck_Lively_II "Dereck Lively II"),[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:192-48) cutting the deficit to 93–90. During this stretch, Dončić fouled out with 4:12 remaining.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:142-42) Lively later scored a dunk to put the Celtics lead at 100–98 until Brown hit a mid-range jump shot with 1:01 left.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:172-46) Sam Quinn of [CBS Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Sports "CBS Sports") retrospectively viewed Brown's shot as "the dagger that won that contest for Boston."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:0-50) From there, Washington, Irving, and [Tim Hardaway Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Hardaway_Jr. "Tim Hardaway Jr.") each missed their three-point attempts as a foul on Tatum with 14.6 seconds left allowed him to make free throws to secure the game and preventing what would have tied the largest comeback from a fourth-quarter deficit in NBA history.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:162-45)
As was done for [Bill Walton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Walton "Bill Walton") prior to Game 1, a moment of silence was held before the game for [Jerry West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_West "Jerry West"), who died earlier that same day at the age of 86. West's silhouette was the basis for the NBA logo, and he was an NBA champion as a player in 1972 with the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") and also a further eight times as an executive with the Lakers and [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-52)

The Mavericks avoided a sweep by the Celtics with a 122–84 blowout victory—the third largest in NBA Finals history—to cut Boston's series lead to 3–1.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:1-53) Luka Dončić led Dallas with 29 points, five rebounds, five assists and three steals. He scored 25 of his total points in the first two quarters, the most ever recorded by a Maverick in a Finals game by halftime.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-54) Kyrie Irving had 21 points and six assists,[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:2-55) and Tim Hardaway Jr. had 15 points off five three-pointers in the fourth quarter, becoming the third player to have scored five threes in a single quarter of a Finals game.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-56) Dereck Lively II had 11 points and 12 rebounds, becoming the second player to achieve multiple double-doubles in the Finals at the age of 20.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:3-57)
Midway through the first quarter, Lively scored his first career three-pointer which gave the Mavericks the lead for the rest of the game.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:1-53) The Mavericks established a 13-point lead by the end of the first,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-58) and a 26-point lead by the half,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:1-53) the fourth largest in Finals history.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:3-57) At halftime, the only Celtics players who made more than one field goal were Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:2-55) The Mavericks continued their momentum into the third quarter, outscoring the Celtics by 15–7 points within the first 4:32. With 3:18 left in the third quarter and the deficit at 36 points, the Celtics ceded defeat by substituting out his starters, which was soon followed by the Mavericks doing the same.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:3-57)
It was the Celtics' largest defeat of the season and their worst overall since the [2017 Eastern Conference Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_NBA_playoffs#Eastern_Conference_finals "2017 NBA playoffs").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:2-55)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-ESPNG5-59) It ended a 10-game postseason winning streak and seven-game road streak, and avoided the chance of them becoming the first team in NBA history to sweep both the Conference Finals and the Finals.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:1-53) The 84 points they scored was the lowest tally of the season,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:3-57) while the game-high 48 points the Mavericks led by was their largest deficit. The 35 points they scored by half was their lowest in two seasons, and the second lowest in a Finals game in franchise history. Tatum and Brown finished with 15 and 10 points respectively.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:1-53)

The Celtics closed out the series in a dominant 106–88 victory at home to claim the NBA championship. Jayson Tatum led them to victory with 31 points, eight rebounds and 11 assists, while Jaylen Brown had 21 points, eight rebounds and six assists.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:16-60) Jrue Holiday, who had 14 points and 11 rebounds,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:16-60) scored the first three field goals of the game for the Celtics.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-YahooG5-61) Playing through an injury that he suffered in Game 2 and sidelined him in Games 3 and 4, Kristaps Porziņģis checked in midway through the first quarter to a standing ovation. He finished with five points in 16 minutes.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-62)
The Mavericks managed to cut the lead to a single point midway through the first quarter, but the Celtics responded with a 12–3 run powered by eight points between Tatum and Brown. Dallas once again attempted a comeback in the second quarter by bringing a 15-point lead down to nine, but Boston proceeded to outscore them 19–7.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:16-60) The Celtics finished the first half with a 21-point lead, which culminated with Payton Pritchard's buzzer-beating half-court shot, the longest made field goal in the Finals since at least 1998.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:17-64) The Mavericks never recovered or led at any point during the game, with the Celtics extending their lead to as much as 26 points in the third quarter.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:17-64) _[Yahoo Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahoo_Sports "Yahoo Sports")_ dubbed the fourth quarter a "[coronation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation "Coronation")" for the Celtics.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-YahooG5-61)
Luka Dončić led the Mavericks with 28 points, 12 rebounds, five assists, and three steals. He missed his first six three-pointers and finished 2 of 9 from that range. Further noted was his poor defensive performance and his seven turnovers.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-YahooG5-61)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-65) Nonetheless, he ended the series averaging 29.2 points, 8.8 rebounds and 5.6 assists, leading all players in points per game.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:24-66) Similar to the first two games, Kyrie Irving struggled and finished with 15 points on 5 of 16 shooting. With Dončić and Irving struggling early the Mavericks had no response.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:17-64)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-YahooG5-61) The Celtics had a 51–35 rebounding advantage and went 17 of 20 (85%) on their free throws line compared to the Mavericks' 7 of 13 (53.8%).[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-YahooG5-61)
With the conclusion of the Finals, Brown was named the [NBA Finals Most Valuable Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player "NBA Finals Most Valuable Player") after averaging 20.8 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 5.0 assists per game. This was in spite of Tatum, generally considered the best player on the Celtics,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:0-50) leading him in most statistical categories with 22.2 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 7.2 assists per game.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:25-67) Brown's performance as the primary defender on Dončić was regarded as a major factor in the series, as he limited his three-point shooting to 24.4% and significantly inhibited his playmaking, with his assists dropping from 9.8 per game in the regular season.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:24-66) Brown also had a higher field goal percentage (44%) compared to Tatum (38.8%) and made important shots throughout the series.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:25-67)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:0-50) Both Brown and Tatum said the winner of the award did not matter to them as their goal was to win the championship, each emphasizing each other's and the team's accomplishment.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:24-66)

## Media coverage
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Media coverage")]
The Finals was televised in the United States by [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_on_ABC "NBA on ABC") (including local affiliates [WCVB-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCVB-TV "WCVB-TV") in Boston and [WFAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WFAA "WFAA") in Dallas) for the 22nd consecutive year. Like before, lead play-by-play broadcaster [Mike Breen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Breen "Mike Breen") and sideline reporter [Lisa Salters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Salters "Lisa Salters") called the NBA Finals.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-Redick-70) With longtime analysts [Jeff Van Gundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Van_Gundy "Jeff Van Gundy") and [Mark Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Jackson "Mark Jackson") being laid off by ESPN,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-72) [Doris Burke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doris_Burke "Doris Burke") and [Doc Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_Rivers "Doc Rivers") were hired as analysts on the lead broadcast team. This made Burke the first woman to serve as a television analyst for a major men's professional championship event.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-Burke-73) The trio of Breen, Burke, and Rivers were to call the NBA Finals.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-Burke-73) However, with Rivers being hired as the head coach of [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks"), [JJ Redick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JJ_Redick "JJ Redick") was enlisted as a replacement to Rivers for the NBA Finals team.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-Redick-70) Following the conclusion of the Finals, however, Redick was hired as head coach of the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-74)
The Finals was broadcast on [ESPN Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_on_ESPN_Radio "NBA on ESPN Radio") with [Marc Kestecher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Kestecher "Marc Kestecher") and [P. J. Carlesimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Carlesimo "P. J. Carlesimo") as commentators, as well as [Jorge Sedano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Sedano "Jorge Sedano") as the reporter. This was the first Finals since [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NBA_Finals "2019 NBA Finals") without Doris Burke as a radio commentator.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-75)

## Impact
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Impact")]
### Celebration
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Celebration")]
[![Image of the Celtics convoy heading down a street during the victory parade in Boston](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Parade_GQnoPTzXcAAjILB.jpg/250px-Parade_GQnoPTzXcAAjILB.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Parade_GQnoPTzXcAAjILB.jpg)The Celtics convoy heading down a street during the victory parade in Boston
Boston Mayor [Michelle Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Wu "Michelle Wu") announced on June 18, 2024, the details for a parade celebrating the Celtics victory, scheduled to take place at 11:00 a.m on June 21. The team would ride the city's traditional ceremonial [duck boats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Duck_Tours "Boston Duck Tours") starting "in front of [TD Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TD_Garden "TD Garden") on Causeway Street, passing by [City Hall Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Hall_Plaza_\(Manchester\) "City Hall Plaza \(Manchester\)") and the [Boston Common](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Common "Boston Common") on [Tremont Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tremont_Street "Tremont Street") and ending on [Boylston Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boylston_Street "Boylston Street") by the [Hynes Convention Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hynes_Convention_Center "Hynes Convention Center")."[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-87) On the scheduled day, the celebration first included a rally at TD Garden featuring the Celtics players and their relatives, organization and arena staff, season ticket holders and notables including Mayor Wu and Massachusetts governor [Maura Healey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maura_Healey "Maura Healey"). The parade then began at 11:15 a.m. and concluded around 90 minutes later. Estimates for the parade's turnout reported at least over 1 million people, with the [MBTA Commuter Rail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MBTA_Commuter_Rail "MBTA Commuter Rail") claiming ridership "on par with 5 days of regular weekday ridership condensed into 5–6 hours."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-88)
### Records and achievements
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Records and achievements")]
[![Image of Al Horford in a Celtics uniform in a basketball game attempting a lay up.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Al_Horford_%2851688343399%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Al_Horford_%2851688343399%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Al_Horford_\(51688343399\)_\(cropped\).jpg)Among the many Celtics who won their first NBA championship is [Al Horford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Horford "Al Horford"), who had previously played 186 playoff games without one.
The Celtics' victory gave them their 18th franchise championship, allowing them to surpass the Los Angeles Lakers, who they were tied with since [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_Finals "2020 NBA Finals"), as the franchise with the [most championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NBA_champions "List of NBA champions") in the NBA.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-apnews.com-89) The victory ended the second-longest franchise drought without a championship at 16 years.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:232-1) The Celtics claimed the 13th championship title this century for a team from the big four sports leagues (the NBA, [MLB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MLB "MLB"), [NFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL "NFL") and [NHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL "NHL")) based in the Boston area.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:16-60) The Celtics were the sixth unique champion team in a row, the longest such parity streak in NBA Finals history since [1975](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_NBA_Finals "1975 NBA Finals")–[1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_NBA_Finals "1980 NBA Finals").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:23-90) It was the first [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") that the Celtics played in that did not go six or seven games since [1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_NBA_Finals "1965 NBA Finals").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-91)
The Celtics finished with a combined 80–21 record including the regular season and the playoffs, and a .792 winning percentage, the second highest in franchise history behind the [1985–86 Celtics season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985%E2%80%9386_Boston_Celtics_season "1985–86 Boston Celtics season").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:16-60) Until their victory, the Celtics played more postseason games over an eight-season span without winning an NBA title than any team in the history of the NBA. With the win, the Celtics finished with the second-best postseason record (16–3) since the NBA went to four best-of-seven rounds of the playoffs in 2003, only behind the [2016–17 Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Golden_State_Warriors_season "2016–17 Golden State Warriors season"), who went 16–1.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-ESPNG5-59)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-93) Speculation arose of the team potentially becoming a [dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_dynasty "Sports dynasty").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:23-90)
Aside from [Jrue Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jrue_Holiday "Jrue Holiday"), who won a title with the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_Milwaukee_Bucks_season "2020–21 Milwaukee Bucks season") in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_Finals "2021 NBA Finals"), every player on the Celtics won their first championship. [Al Horford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Horford "Al Horford") set a record for the most playoff games without an NBA championship before winning one with 186.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-apnews.com-89) Only [Karl Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Malone "Karl Malone") has played more career playoff games (193) without winning a championship.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-94) Tatum and Brown's 107 playoff games played together represent the most by a duo prior to winning their first championship in NBA history.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:16-60) Among the many international players on the Celtics, Horford, Porziņģis and [Neemias Queta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neemias_Queta "Neemias Queta") represent the first Dominican-,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-95) Latvian-,[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-96) and Portuguese-born[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-97) players respectively to win a championship. For the coaching staff, this represented head coach [Joe Mazzulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla "Joe Mazzulla"), and assistant coaches [Anthony Dobbins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Dobbins "Anthony Dobbins"), [Amile Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amile_Jefferson "Amile Jefferson"), [D. J. MacLeay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._J._MacLeay "D. J. MacLeay") and [Matt Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Reynolds_\(basketball\) "Matt Reynolds \(basketball\)")'s first NBA championship—as well as the second for [Charles Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Lee_\(basketball\) "Charles Lee \(basketball\)") (2021), and fourth for [Sam Cassell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Cassell "Sam Cassell") ([1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_NBA_Finals "1994 NBA Finals"), [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_NBA_Finals "1995 NBA Finals"), 2008 as a player). It also represented the first championship for 2023–24 [NBA Executive of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Executive_of_the_Year_Award "NBA Executive of the Year Award") winner [Brad Stevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Stevens "Brad Stevens"), and the culmination of a ten-year rebuild that began when he originally joined the Celtics in 2013 as the head coach.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-98)
The NBA playoff pool was at a record $33,657,947 (USD), which is distributed to each of the [16 playoff teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs "2024 NBA playoffs"). Boston's share of the NBA's playoff pool prior to the victory was $7,202,498. By clinching the championship they tacked on another $4,856,937 in winnings, bringing their total to $12,059,435, the most a team has ever won from the postseason bonus money pool. Dallas' share ended up at $5,899,422.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-apnews.com-89)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-99) The victory triggered a contractual bonus of $1,183,200 for Holiday.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-100) In total, Holiday's achievements in his first season with the Celtics netted him around $2.8 million, which represents every incentive bonus in his contract.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-101)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-102)
Playing for the [US Men's Basketball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_basketball_team "United States men's national basketball team") later that summer, [Jrue Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jrue_Holiday "Jrue Holiday"), [Jayson Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") and [Derrick White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_White "Derrick White") would join [Khris Middleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khris_Middleton "Khris Middleton") (2021), [Kyrie Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrie_Irving "Kyrie Irving") (2016), [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") (2012), [Scottie Pippen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottie_Pippen "Scottie Pippen") (1996, 1992) and [Michael Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") (1992) as the only players to win an NBA Finals and Olympic gold medal in the same year. Holiday also joined Pippen as the only players to accomplish this feat twice.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-103)
## Aftermath
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Aftermath")]
### Celtics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Celtics")]
[![Image of Wyc Grousbeck and Joe Biden holding the Larry O'Brien trophy at the White House while surrounded by Celtics players.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/P20241121ES-0980_%2854157603844%29.jpg/250px-P20241121ES-0980_%2854157603844%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:P20241121ES-0980_\(54157603844\).jpg)Owner [Wyc Grousbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyc_Grousbeck "Wyc Grousbeck") and United States president [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") holding the [Larry O'Brien trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_O'Brien_Championship_Trophy "Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy") during the Celtics visit to the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") in 2024.
On July 1, 2024, fifteen days after winning the championship, Celtics owner [Wyc Grousbeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyc_Grousbeck "Wyc Grousbeck") put the team up for sale.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-104) In March 2025, they were sold for $6.1 billion to a group led by private equity executive [Bill Chisholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Chisholm_\(businessman\) "Bill Chisholm \(businessman\)").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-105) It was the largest sale of an NBA franchise until the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") surpassed the mark a few months later.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-106)
The Celtics were unable to defend their NBA title the next season despite being favourites to do so, making it the seventh straight season the NBA did not have a repeat champion—the longest such stretch in league history. Boston was defeated in the [Eastern Conference semifinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NBA_playoffs#\(2\)_Boston_Celtics_vs._\(3\)_New_York_Knicks "2025 NBA playoffs") by the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_New_York_Knicks_season "2024–25 New York Knicks season") in six games, during which [Jayson Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") tore his [Achilles tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:21-107) With key players such as Al Horford, Kristaps Porziņģis, and Luke Kornet leaving the team in the offseason, the [2025–26 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Boston_Celtics_season "2025–26 Boston Celtics season") was expected by some to be a "gap year". The new roster exceeded expectations and the Celtics finished as the second seed, with Jaylen Brown being viewed as a MVP candidate and Tatum returning from his injury ahead of schedule in March. They were eliminated by the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Philadelphia_76ers_season "2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season") in the [first round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_playoffs "2026 NBA playoffs") of the playoffs in seven games after blowing a [3–1 series lead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_teams_that_have_overcome_3%E2%80%930_series_deficits "List of teams that have overcome 3–0 series deficits").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-108) This ended the [Jays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jays_\(Boston_Celtics\) "Jays \(Boston Celtics\)")-era for the Celtics, as [Jaylen Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Brown "Jaylen Brown") was traded to the 76ers for [Paul George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_George "Paul George") and draft pick compensation in the off-season.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-109)
### Mavericks
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_NBA_Finals&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Mavericks")]
See also: [Luka Dončić–Anthony Davis trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Don%C4%8Di%C4%87%E2%80%93Anthony_Davis_trade "Luka Dončić–Anthony Davis trade")
> [Jayson Tatum] is the reason why Luka got traded. He shut him down in the finals. What he did to Luka in the Finals, shutting him down, guarding him full court, making it unbearable offensively, led Dallas to start questioning Luka as the leader of the team, and questioning whether he was in shape or not.
— NBA insider Marc Spears
Luka Dončić received criticism for his defensive performance during the Finals despite his offensive prowess.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:22-110) [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") sportswriter [Brian Windhorst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Windhorst "Brian Windhorst") harshly criticized his defense and complaining to officials during Game 3, calling it "unacceptable" and stating it was costing the Mavericks the series. Windhorst said, "If Luka's ever gonna be a winner... he's gonna have to use [this Finals] as a learning experience".[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-111)
The following [2024–25 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_NBA_season "2024–25 NBA season"), the Mavericks traded away Dončić to the Los Angeles Lakers for [Anthony Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Davis "Anthony Davis") in [a highly publicized midseason trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Don%C4%8Di%C4%87%E2%80%93Anthony_Davis_trade "Luka Dončić–Anthony Davis trade").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-112) Windhorst suggested the Mavericks were displeased by Dončić's performance in the Finals as he was never confronted by members of the organization after his Game 3 comments.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-113) NBA insider Marc Spears cited Jayson Tatum's performance against Dončić on both ends as the catalyst to the Mavericks rethinking their commitment to him.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-:22-110)
Injuries to Davis and Kyrie Irving led to the Mavericks becoming the first team since the [2019–20 Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Golden_State_Warriors_season "2019–20 Golden State Warriors season") to miss the playoffs after reaching the NBA Finals the previous season.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-114) The Mavericks received the first overall pick in the [2025 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NBA_draft "2025 NBA draft"), against 1.8 percent [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") odds, and took star forward [Cooper Flagg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooper_Flagg "Cooper Flagg"). General manager [Nico Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Harrison "Nico Harrison") was fired following a poor start to the [2025–26 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Dallas_Mavericks_season "2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season") and enduring fan backlash to the Dončić trade.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals#cite_note-115)
